title: On-Device Intelligence Empowers People with Disabilities and Smart Interaction Scenarios
summary: vivo's on-device accessibility suite offers offline speech, vision and sign language features; its sign language avatar scored 3.513 of 5 in a 2024 shared task, against 2.119 for the baseline.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: vivo reports that it released vivo Sight, a visual assistance product, in 2023. It reports that it listed an upgraded version for vivo phone users in May 2024. In the CCL24-Eval shared task of July 2024, organizers from Beijing Union University and Xiamen University had deaf sign language users and certified translators rate the four sign language avatar systems that passed screening. They ranked vivo's system first with 3.513 of 5, against 2.119 for the baseline. The shared task measured the quality of avatar output on four test sentences. In its project account for the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, vivo describes on-device speech, vision and sign language features that work offline. vivo reports direct accessibility benefits for users. No source measures everyday use or the wider social effects.
purpose: Help disabled and multilingual users communicate and access information offline.

ratings.reason: vivo reports offline speech, vision and sign language assistance that expands communication and access to information. Its user figures do not establish lasting outcomes for every user.
vivo asserts a 90% reduction in cloud energy use. No source measures the total energy use of devices and cloud or the net environmental effect.

evidence.citation: Yuan Zhao, Ruiquan Zhang, Dengfeng Yao and Yidong Chen, Overview of CCL24-Eval Task 10: Translation Quality Evaluation of Sign Language Avatar, Proceedings of the 23rd China National Conference on Computational Linguistics, Volume 3: Evaluations, pages 405 to 415, July 2024. Organizers from Beijing Union University, Xiamen University and Tsinghua University, funded by national science and language grants, ran a shared task in which deaf sign language users and certified sign language translators rated the four of ten submitted systems that passed preliminary screening. They have no stake in vivo. Their test measures output quality on four test sentences and has no measure of everyday use.
